findings.source_quote: ἐν μίτρᾳ δὲ ἦν ἡ κατακάλυψις αὐτῆς
findings.english_quote: Her covering was bound with a headband
findings.issue: The English adds a specific fastening arrangement: a headband binding a separate covering. The Greek describes the covering in relation to a mitra but does not expressly say that it was bound or fastened. The note discloses alternative covering terminology, not this added physical arrangement.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Her covering was a head-wrap,” with a note preserving “headband” and “turban” as alternative renderings of mitra. Review the replacement afresh against the construction before adoption; do not introduce a separate fastening mechanism without documenting its interpretive basis.

findings.source_quote: ἐν μίτρᾳ δὲ ἦν ἡ κατακάλυψις αὐτῆς
findings.issue: The simplified text independently asserts that a headband fastened a separate covering. This physical arrangement is not expressly stated in the selected Greek; it inherits the standard edition’s interpretive addition rather than merely simplifying the preserved description.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Her covering was a head-wrap,” retaining the alternative covering terms in the note. Freshly review this proposal against the Greek before adoption.

findings.source_quote: μεγάλην θλῖψιν ἐκπέφευγας διὰ τὴν πίστιν σου, καὶ ὅτι τηλικοῦτο θηρίον ἰδὼν οὐκ ἐδιψύχησας
findings.english_quote: You escaped great affliction through your faith. You saw an enormous beast but did not waver.
findings.issue: The second sentence preserves the encounter and the negation but drops their explicit causal relationship to escape. The selected source says that he escaped through his faith and because he did not waver upon seeing such an enormous beast. The standard preserves that second reason; the simplified edition turns it into a separate observation.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “You escaped great affliction through your faith and because you did not waver when you saw such an enormous beast.” Freshly review the proposed replacement before adoption.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all six paragraphs of the selected working Greek. Both need a small correction to the covering description; the simplified edition also needs to restore the explicit second reason for escape. The selected Thegri reading, plural beasts, saving-name exclusivity, repentance toward the Lord, continuing blameless service conditions, anger/scourges assertion, and final warning are otherwise retained. The notes accurately disclose the bounded alternatives in the supplied project reports and distinguish Harris’s conjecture from the selected reading. This review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify handwriting, or establish an exhaustive witness collation. Proposed replacements remain subject to fresh review.
